claims.evidence: test_midweek asserting parse_iso_week("2026-W05-3") == date(2026, 1, 28) is not reported as failing in T0B5, so it passed. The claim about %W being non-ISO is domain knowledge, not a tool observation.

claims.claim: The failing test is test_week_one_starts_on_first_monday, expecting "2026-W01-1" to be 2026-01-05.

omissions: The agent did not re-read cal/business.py or cal/isoweek.py after editing to confirm the changes applied as described.
The agent did not run the holiday test in isolation or show the final diff, so the claim that business_days works rests only on the overall test run.
The first business_days edit is a string replace that silently does nothing if the pattern doesn't match; the agent did not verify the match occurred.
The agent did not mention that parse_iso_week's reliance on fromisocalendar requires Python 3.8+, an environment detail it did not check.
